newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU may allow shops to charge for payment by card.
newsitem.headline: EU may allow shops to charge for payment by card.

text.p: The European Commission may rule soon that European Union shops should be allowed to discriminate against payments made with credit and other cards as opposed to cash.
The expected decision is a blow for the banking industry which currently forces retailers in most EU countries to charge the same price whatever the means of payment.
"The Commission has doubts about this rule; it would like it to disappear," a Commission spokesman told a news briefing in reply to a question about a report in French newspaper Liberation.

Scrapping the non-discriminatory rule would increase competition between payment systems and allow retailers to negotiate better service fees with card companies or banks issuing their own debit and credit cards, the spokesman for European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said.
He rejected the suggestion that the move would spell bad news for consumers. But the European consumer organisation BEUC was divided on the issue, he conceded.
The rule imposed by credit card companies, represented by Brussels-based Europay, is already illegal in Britain, Belgium, Sweden and the Netherlands.
In Belgium, retailers charge customers an extra five francs (14 cents) each time they pay with a debit card. $1 = 35 Belgian francs -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841
